A new TrendForce analysis estimates that the parts Apple pays for in the iPhone 18 Pro will cost 38% more than the previous generation. Unsurprisingly, the biggest increase is in memory costs, with Apple reportedly paying roughly triple what it has in the past this year.

However, the firm's analysis supports my personal view that this year's price hikes won't be as steep as some are anticipating…

iPhone 18 Pro parts costs rise 38%

The cost of producing a new device can broadly be divided into three parts: components, assembly, and operating expenses. The last of these covers everything from R&D for the new device through to marketing campaigns.

TrendForce's report focuses specifically on the first part, what's known as the Bill of Materials (BOM).

The report notes that while memory accounted for only about 10% of iPhone parts costs last year, it's expected to exceed 40% by next year.

This is a major shift. In the past year, the display was still the most expensive component in the iPhone; this year, memory will take over.

But Apple will likely absorb some of the costs itself

Two sources have recently pointed to a $1,399 starting price for this year's iPhone 18 Pro. And the latest estimates of Apple's production costs could indeed support that level of price increase.

However, I wrote last week that this is unlikely, and that Apple will probably choose to absorb some of the increased costs itself in order to maintain market demand.

TrendForce agrees with this view, citing the example of Apple's MacBook price hikes. While the increases have already been quite significant, they still don't fully reflect the actual rise in Apple's manufacturing costs.

The firm also agrees with Bloomberg's take that Apple will very likely raise the price of the iPhone 17 Pro before next month's launch event. This morning may be your last chance to follow Chance's advice and buy one right away.
